slices.title: quiet-stacked-exemplar
slices.summary: Accepted one reversible economics exemplar for delayed human review: page-colored stacked stage, stable rails, one phase-derived passage salience scalar, full-focused active prose, and quieter upcoming prose. No shared motif promotion or split-layout changes.

slices.title: startup-attribution
slices.summary: Reproduced and attributed startup debt without product changes: 255232 B transfer, 152720 B script, 42 resources, one 180 ms startup task; active motion remains healthy at 34.7 ms p95, zero active long tasks/CLS/SVG rebuilds. Evidence orders static publication, CSS ownership, fixed-route closure, and font/theme work.

slices.title: static-narrative-shell
slices.summary: Published the complete ordered economics narrative into production route HTML for no-JavaScript readers: headings, 11 passages, TOC links, stable section/block/checkpoint IDs, and build-time KaTeX HTML/MathML. Current enhanced presenter remains unchanged; stage adoption is reserved for r04-r05.

slices.title: static-stage-shell
slices.summary: Published one deterministic initial economics SVG plus reserved progress and native scrub geometry in route HTML. Static and runtime graphs share the exact viewport/axis shell. The route artifact grew to 8.15 KB gzip, while client entry remained at 183.39 KB raw rather than downloading duplicate markup.

slices.title: progressive-enhancement-boundary
slices.summary: Published route HTML is now the real searchable document. The Svelte-free ?enhancement=published path adopts the exact prose, IDs, controls, and SVG, uses one retained runtime and clock, restores semantic hashes directly, and downloads no duplicate compiled prose; the default legacy presenter is isolated for r08.

slices.title: tutorial-foundation-css
slices.summary: Isolated minimal framework neutral tutorial foundation CSS closed global stylesheet ownership for the economics public entry preserved all focused and browser checks and measured the remaining pre r10 fixed route budget debt.

slices.title: graph-domain-css-split
slices.summary: Split graph styling into route scoped graph surface dimensional continuity economics equilibrium and demand shift lesson owners with exact cascade visual and build preservation.

slices.title: presenter-route-closure
slices.summary: Public economics now defaults to the published progressive capability. The optional 180.25 kB presenter, 669.42 kB CodeMirror runtime, and per-layout CSS remain dynamic; direct layout URLs, one-runtime transitions, and publication restoration are browser verified.

slices.title: font-theme-closure
slices.summary: Source Serif 300 is discovered and preloaded before publication paint, the route owns one standalone theme sheet, static prose and graph use semantic light and midnight tokens, and editor fonts stay out of the learner closure with no measured CLS.

slices.title: publication-performance-gate
slices.summary: The production gate now measures the published learner route: 135252 B transfer, 99029 B script, 29 resources, zero CLS, 1.5-1.7 ms active p95, no active long tasks, retained graph nodes, and a 120-mutation ceiling after removing redundant custom-element text writes. Presenter and CodeMirror capabilities remain outside startup.

slices.title: whole-lesson-buffer-schema
slices.summary: Added one economics-local, layout-neutral whole-lesson buffer with deterministic Markdown-like typed directives for lesson, stage, motion-passage, passage, motion-block, and semantic-reference identities. The current six-passage compiled narrative reconstructs exactly; escaping, reorder, schema version, ownership, and executable-source rejection are verified.

slices.title: incremental-last-valid-preview
slices.summary: Added a framework-neutral debounced whole-buffer preview session. It recompiles only changed passages, preserves the last valid preview and one stage-session identity through invalid edits, emits deterministic diagnostics, and restores the nearest surviving passage ID after structural edits.

slices.title: semantic-repository-completion
slices.summary: Replaced the hard-coded completion list with a lazy repository-backed semantic index covering actual lesson, stage, passage, motion-block, checkpoint, animation, stage-object, reference, and transit IDs. CodeMirror now provides contextual kp-ref, directive, and ID completion plus stale-reference diagnostics; no fictitious vignette contract was introduced.

slices.title: reversible-passage-commands
slices.summary: Added pure complete-buffer transactions for add, duplicate, move, confirmed delete, and source update. Commands preserve stable IDs, strip copied semantic authority, protect motion/reference owners, and return one replacement suitable for CodeMirror's sole undo/redo history.

slices.title: practical-editor-chrome
slices.summary: Replaced per-passage editing with one large whole-lesson CodeMirror/Vim buffer. The editor now exposes dirty, validity, save, selected-passage, modeline, and native ex state; structural operations enter CodeMirror's sole history; invalid source retains the last valid preview; q/w/wq, local recovery, source save, and focus return are verified while the public reader remains isolated.

slices.title: semantic-toc-publication
slices.summary: Published one hierarchical TOC containing lesson sections and motion-passage starts but no scrub moments. Complete light DOM and native links remain useful without JavaScript; a native details disclosure is compact on mobile and expanded on wide/no-JS views; the progressive host opts into sparse IntersectionObserver active-heading projection while presenter hosts retain their own semantic authority.

slices.title: direct-navigation-transaction
slices.summary: Published and presenter economics hosts now share the state-before-viewport navigation transaction. Cold deep links, TOC clicks, and history restore exact semantic frames directly without replay; typed previous/next, skip, settle, and exit actions resolve stable block, checkpoint, or section IDs through the same controller, while final navigation chrome remains deferred.

slices.title: no-js-accessibility-hardening
slices.summary: The published route now exposes one checkpoint-driven polite graph-state description, implements its advertised Alt+Arrow semantic checkpoint commands without capturing editable fields, and has a dedicated browser gate for searchable no-JavaScript phone navigation, native disclosure, reduced motion, forced colors, visible focus, and semantic graph/control roles. Provisional layout choreography is unchanged.
